newsitem.title: UK: Safeway, BP link up to offer "food and fuel" stops.
newsitem.headline: Safeway, BP link up to offer "food and fuel" stops.

text.p: British supermarket retailer Safeway Plc joined forces with British Petroleum (BP) on Friday to invest 100 million pounds ($156.9 million) in developing "food and fuel" shopping and petrol retail sites in the UK.
The move, which comes amid a fierce petrol price war between supermarket groups and oil majors, will target around 100 sites in prime locations, the companies said.
The sites will be laid out to offer dedicated parking along with separate store access for pedestrians.
"We believe there is a rapidly growing demand for this style of combined retail outlet," Rolf Stomberg, chief executive of BP Oil, said in a statement.
A pilot site at a Safeway store in Basildon, eastern England, will open next month with further sites planned for early 1997, the companies said.
If they are successful, a countrywide development will start. Profits from the venture will be shared equally between the two companies.
The petrol facilities will be BP branded while the shops will carry Safeway's logo, with poles outside sporting the colours of both companies.
The sites for the stores will be picked from the network of 2,000 service stations created from the recent merger of BP and Mobil's European retail business.

The move picks up on a growing trend for supermarkets to offer petrol sales at larger stores while petrol majors have increasingly expanded the amount of food offered at their station sites. ($1=.6373 Pound)
